domain_label: Realism & Anti-AI QC Protocol — Per-Shot Checklist, Luxury Physics, Mitigation Map, Compression Honesty
purpose: A method for the QC work an expert performs to satisfy the owner's number-one requirement ('it should not look AI - natural, realistic, physics and all'): running an ordered per-shot noticeability checklist against generated stills and video, applying luxury-specific physics checks (wheels, glass/liquid, fabric, jewelry, water, golden-hour shadows), routing every flagged tell through a mitigation map (prompt / model-choice / re-roll / post / shot-redesign), avoiding or working around a known-hard shot list, and weighting all of it honestly against what social-platform compression and phone-screen viewing actually hide versus reveal - grounded against the research file's FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN tags, never inventing a benchmark number, a study result, or a Higgsfield-surface detail this KB does not own.
assumptions: no live shot-outcome dataset or per-model failure ledger is supplied; every score is a heuristic prior, and every cited number is quoted from the grounding research file's tagged sources, not re-derived here

the research file's own grounding note is carried forward honestly: the egress proxy 403-blocked every direct WebFetch attempted, so citations rest on WebSearch result excerpts of named papers/guides and Hugging Face paper_search abstracts; a claim tagged [FACT - via search excerpt] in the research file keeps that tag here rather than being upgraded to a directly-verified fact

the noticeability ordering of the ten-item rubric, the 0/1/2 scoring gate, and the re-roll/post-fix thresholds are editorial syntheses [ESTIMATE] built from the prevalence of cues across forensic guides and the physics-benchmark failure severities, not a fetched ranking study - no such ranking study was found this session

contested or replication-flagged psychology findings (e.g., the no-training 48.2% baseline in Nightingale & Farid, exact Ebbinghaus/Cepeda/Roediger effect sizes) keep the confidence caveat or UNKNOWN tag the research file assigned; they are never restated as settled fact

the likeness closed-lane stays closed: this KB gives no guidance for evoking a specific real person's identity while concealing or altering the face; identity-lock content here concerns only a studio-created persona's own self-consistency across shots

which Higgsfield model/mode names support first-frame or last-frame conditioning is out of scope for this KB and left [UNKNOWN here] pending the MCP-surface research file; no Higgsfield model name, id, parameter, duration, or aspect ratio is stated in this KB because none is sourced from higgsfield_surface.md here
exclusions: which specific Higgsfield model/mode to select for a given shot, its parameters, durations, aspect ratios, or credit cost - that belongs to the MCP-surface specialist grounded in higgsfield_surface.md
disclosure/labeling obligations (e.g., platform AI-content labels) and legal/policy compliance - that belongs to the media-manager or legal-scope specialist
the persona/character-design specialist's job of building the reference sheet itself; this KB only specifies that identity must be diffed against it
engagement, virality, or audience-response prediction; this KB is a realism/physics QC gate only, not a performance-prediction system

competency_questions.question: What is the ordered per-shot QC checklist and why is it ordered the way it is?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PER_SHOT_RUBRIC_ORDER lists all ten rubric items from most to least noticeable (text/logos, hands, contact physics, identity, object permanence, shadow/reflection, motion quality, texture stability, background coherence, skin micro-texture), states the three checkpoints they apply at, and names the ordering as an editorial synthesis, not a fetched ranking

competency_questions.question: What is the per-item scoring scale and the gate threshold that forces a re-roll versus allows a post-only fix?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RUBRIC_SCORING_GATE gives the 0/1/2 scale, states any single 2 or a total >=4 forces a re-roll, and that a total of 2-3 with no single 2 is fixable in post only if the offending region is croppable/gradeable/speed-rampable

competency_questions.question: What do human deepfake-detection studies actually show numerically, and what operational reading follows?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HUMAN_DETECTION_BASELINE cites Diel et al. 2024 (55.54% overall, 57.31% video), Groh et al. PNAS 2022 (~66%, 73% with model assist), Nightingale & Farid PNAS 2022 (59.0% trained, synthetic faces rated more trustworthy), and Miller et al. 2023 (69.5% vs 52.2%, Dunning-Kruger pattern), and draws the worst-artifact-driven per-shot conclusion rather than 'humans can't tell so QC doesn't matter'

competency_questions.question: Why can't an automated VLM/MLLM QC critic be the sole gate?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DETECTOR_LIMITATION cites Artifact-Bench's finding that many of 19 evaluated MLLMs performed near or below random and that MLLM judgments significantly misalign with human perceptual preference, concluding a human must remain in the QC loop

competency_questions.question: What is the text/logo/badge tell and why does it rank first?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TEXT_LOGO_TELL states garbled lettering/near-English text is historically the most reliable single tell, that clean typography does not prove real, and that luxury brand logos/badges are high-risk because viewers know exactly what they should look like

competency_questions.question: What are the hand-motion and contact-physics tells specific to video, and how do the physics benchmarks quantify contact-physics failure?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HAND_MOTION_TELL states finger morphing and held-object blending as a strengthening-in-video tell despite weakening in stills, and CONTACT_PHYSICS_TELL cites VideoPhy's 39.6% best-model pass rate and VideoPhy-2's 22% hard-subset figure for conservation-law failures at contact points

competency_questions.question: What is identity drift, and how must a studio persona be checked for self-consistency across shots?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: IDENTITY_LOCK_TELL names identity drift as an industry-documented phenomenon, requires diffing every shot's persona attributes against the master reference sheet (not just the adjacent shot), and names locking identity at an approved start frame as the strongest structural mitigation

competency_questions.question: What are the shadow/reflection geometry tell and the second-order motion/acceleration tell, and what do the physics benchmarks say about each?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SHADOW_REFLECTION_TELL states the single-light-source shadow-direction and reflection-vanishing-point forensic checks, and MOTION_QUALITY_TELL cites D3's second-order feature divergence finding and NSG-VD's spatiotemporal-deviation finding plus Sora's stated physics-and-complex-action limitation

competency_questions.question: What luxury-specific physics checks must be applied to wheels, glass/liquid, fabric, jewelry, water, and golden-hour light, and what is each one's common AI failure?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: each of the six luxury-physics nodes states the must-be-true physical condition, the common AI failure mode, and its grounding, including the wagon-wheel stroboscopic caveat and the single-sun-parallel-shadow rule

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMPRESSION_HONESTY states compression hides frequency fingerprints, skin micro-texture waxiness and faint boiling/shimmer, does NOT hide garbled logos/finger counts/foot sliding/shadow errors/identity drift/object-count changes, flags the small-screen quantification as UNKNOWN, and states the phone-screen-final-QC doctrine

glossary.definition: A documented category of visual or temporal error (improper fur/hair flow, unrealistic corneal reflections, anatomically impossible joints, illogical shadow geometry, etc.) that forensic reviews use to classify AI-generated stills [FACT - arXiv 2502.15176 review taxonomy, via search excerpt].

A three-level hierarchical taxonomy for AI-video realism (top-level domains: temporal inconsistencies, structural distortions, semantic incoherence -> mid-level failure families -> 30 fine-grained artifact types); it also evaluated 19 leading MLLMs on artifact spotting, finding many near or below random and significantly misaligned with human perceptual preference [FACT - arXiv 2605.18984 abstract via Hugging Face paper_search].

The D3 finding that AI-generated video diverges from real video in Newtonian second-order (acceleration) feature distributions even when frame-to-frame position looks plausible, enabling training-free detection with a +10.39pp mAP gain over prior best on GenVideo [FACT - arXiv 2508.00701 abstract].

A benchmark scoring whether generated video adheres to both its caption and physical law; the best tested model (CogVideoX-5B) passed only 39.6% of instances, with solid-fluid and fluid-fluid interactions curated as failure-prone; the harder VideoPhy-2 subset dropped the best model to 22% joint performance [FACT - arXiv 2406.03520 and 2503.06800 abstracts].

The industry-named phenomenon of a generated character's face geometry, eye color, or wardrobe changing across frames or shots without a scripted cause [FACT - via search excerpts, Kling.ai blog and DZone].

The effect by which social-platform recompression 'launders' low-level forensic cues - destroying frequency fingerprints and micro-texture statistics that detectors and careful viewers rely on - while leaving semantic and geometric tells (garbled text, wrong finger counts, shadow errors) intact [FACT - via search excerpts of compressed-deepfake-detection papers, S18].

The per-shot QC score: each of ten noticeability-ordered tells is rated 0 (clean) / 1 (visible on inspection) / 2 (visible at a glance); any single 2 or a running total of 4 or more forces a re-roll [ESTIMATE - editorial operationalization of the noticeability synthesis, no fetched study specifies this exact scale].

The reasoning that a luxury audience's car, watch, and jewelry experts detect object-specific physics errors (wheel stance, bezel glint, badge geometry) at a higher rate than the roughly 55% general-population deepfake-detection baseline, so those objects deserve disproportionate QC attention [ESTIMATE - audience reasoning built on the Diel et al. 2024 baseline, moderate-high confidence].

A shot category (eating/drinking, dexterous hand-object manipulation, gymnastics/fast choreography, feet-prominent walking, legible text/badges, mirrors showing the subject, crowds, hero fluid pours) documented as an open generation-research problem, for which shot redesign - not further iteration - is the reliable fix [FACT - S14 Sora-limitation and hand-object-interaction research, S4 VideoPhy fluid classes, S8-S11 forensic-guide tells].

nodes.definition: State the actual human-detection numbers so QC priorities are evidence-based rather than assumed. Diel et al. 2024 (Computers in Human Behavior: AI; 56 papers, 86,155 participants): overall deepfake-detection accuracy 55.54% (95% CI 48.87-62.10, crossing chance); by modality video 57.31%, images 53.16%, audio 62.08%, text 52.00% [FACT - via search excerpt]. Groh et al. PNAS 2022 (15,016 participants): ~66% accuracy on deepfake face video, rising to 73% when participants saw a model's prediction first [FACT - via search excerpt]. Nightingale & Farid PNAS 2022: trained-with-feedback accuracy on real-vs-GAN faces reached only 59.0% (95% CI 57.7-60.4), and synthetic faces were rated MORE trustworthy than real (4.82 vs 4.48 on a 7-point scale) [FACT - via search excerpt]; the widely reported no-training baseline of 48.2% (below chance) is carried at [ESTIMATE - high-but-not-fetched confidence, primary PDF proxy-blocked]. Miller et al. 2023: AI White faces judged human 69.5% of the time versus 52.2% for real White human faces, with the most-confident raters making the MOST errors (a Dunning-Kruger pattern) [FACT - via search excerpts]. Net operational reading: static face realism is a mostly-won battle, and while humans are barely above chance in aggregate one-shot judgments, an account posting repeatedly means one blatant tell can flip perceived authenticity permanently - so QC must be per-shot and worst-artifact-driven, not average-quality-driven.

included: the four fetched human-detection studies and their headline numbers
excluded: the automated-VLM-critic limitation (its own node)
the per-shot rubric itself (its own node)

failure_modes: treating the low aggregate one-shot accuracy as evidence that QC doesn't matter

nodes.definition: Establish why an automated VLM/MLLM-based QC critic is useful but insufficient alone. Artifact-Bench evaluated 19 leading multimodal LLMs on artifact spotting in AI-generated video: many performed near or below random in challenging settings, and MLLM judgments significantly misaligned with human perceptual preference [FACT - abstract via Hugging Face paper_search]. Consequence for the pipeline: a VLM-based automated pass can pre-filter obvious failures cheaply and at scale, but it cannot be the only gate - a human (or at minimum a person deliberately applying the ordered rubric) must sit in the feedback loop before a shot is declared clean, because the detector's blind spots do not reliably match either the physics-benchmark failure modes or the audience's actual noticing pattern from HUMAN_DETECTION_BASELINE.

excluded: the specific rubric a human applies (its own node)
the checkpoint structure of the full QC loop (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: Artifact-Bench or a successor benchmark reports MLLM artifact-judgment accuracy improving materially

pros.claim: An automated critic pre-filter is cheap and can catch some obvious failures before human review time is spent
pros.example: auto-rejecting a shot with an obviously melted background before a human reviewer even opens it

cons.claim: Trusting the automated critic's verdict as final risks shipping a shot with a tell the MLLM missed but a human audience would not
cons.example: an MLLM passing a shot with a garbled watch-face logo because its artifact judgment misaligns with human perception

failure_modes: shipping a shot solely on an automated critic's pass verdict
assuming MLLM artifact-spotting accuracy scales with general MLLM capability improvements without re-testing
acceptance_tests: the analysis cites the Artifact-Bench MLLM evaluation finding and states a human must remain in the QC loop rather than the critic alone
revisit_triggers: Artifact-Bench or a successor benchmark reports MLLM artifact-judgment accuracy improving materially

nodes.definition: Define the ten-item per-shot QC checklist ordered by human noticeability, the operational answer to the owner's number-one requirement. Order, most to least noticeable: (1) text/logos/badges, (2) hands in motion, (3) contact physics (foot slide, wheel slip, splash-from-nothing), (4) identity lock, (5) object permanence and count, (6) shadow/reflection geometry, (7) motion quality (accelerations), (8) texture stability (boiling/shimmer), (9) background coherence, (10) skin micro-texture. Ordering rationale carried honestly: no fetched study ranks cue noticeability directly; the order is an editorial synthesis from the prevalence and emphasis across forensic guides, the physics-benchmark failure severities, and the finding that faces pass while motion fails [ESTIMATE - moderate-high confidence]. Apply the checklist at three checkpoints: the start-frame image (items 1, 4, 5, 6, 9, 10), the raw generated video (all ten items), and the post-edited reel (items 1-4 at final resolution on a phone screen, since compression can mask items 7-10).

included: the three checkpoints and which items apply at each
the editorial-synthesis honesty caveat on the ordering
excluded: the 0/1/2 scoring scale and re-roll thresholds (its own node)
the content of each individual tell (their own nodes)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a fetched noticeability ranking study supersedes the editorial ordering synthesis

pros.claim: An explicit noticeability order lets limited QC time be spent where it matters most instead of evenly across all ten items
pros.example: checking a shot's logo and hands thoroughly while giving skin micro-texture only a glance, because the former are near-instantly noticeable and the latter is compression-masked anyway

cons.claim: Because the order is an editorial synthesis rather than a fetched ranking study, it can misrank an item for a specific shot type
cons.example: a shot whose only flaw is a subtle background tile-repeat being under-scrutinized because background coherence ranks ninth

failure_modes: applying the ten items in arbitrary order and diluting QC attention evenly
presenting the editorial ordering as if it were a fetched, validated ranking study
acceptance_tests: the analysis lists all ten items in noticeability order, states the three checkpoints and their item subsets, and names the ordering as an editorial synthesis

nodes.definition: Score each of the ten rubric items 0 = clean, 1 = visible on inspection, 2 = visible at a glance. Gate: any single item scoring 2 forces a re-roll regardless of the total; a running total of 4 or more forces a re-roll; a total of 2-3 with no single item at 2 is fixable in post only if the offending region is croppable, gradeable, or speed-rampable (see MITIGATION_MAP); a total of 0-1 passes outright. This scale and gate are an editorial operationalization of the noticeability ordering, not a numeric finding from any fetched source [ESTIMATE - editorial operationalization]; the any-single-2 override exists because HUMAN_DETECTION_BASELINE shows one glaring tell can flip an account's perceived authenticity permanently even when average shot quality is fine.

included: the any-single-2 and total>=4 re-roll rules

cons.claim: A fixed numeric gate can be gamed or misapplied if a reviewer computes the total before checking the any-single-2 override

treating a total of 2-3 as automatically post-fixable without checking whether the offending region is actually croppable or gradeable

nodes.definition: Carry the compression and small-screen factor honestly into QC weighting. Social platforms recompress aggressively; deepfake-forensics literature is explicit that this 'launders low-level forensic cues' - block effects obscure artifacts, textural information is lost, and detectors trained on clean data degrade badly on platform-compressed video [FACT - via search excerpts]. Compression HIDES: generator frequency fingerprints and upsampling signatures [FACT - S1/S18], skin micro-texture waxiness, faint boiling/shimmer, and film-grain absence [ESTIMATE - these are high-frequency phenomena of the same kind compression removes, high confidence]. Compression does NOT hide: garbled logos, wrong finger counts, foot sliding, shadow-direction errors, identity drift, and object-count changes - these are semantic/geometric, survive any bitrate, and are the cues human raters use anyway [ESTIMATE - reasoned from what compression removes versus preserves, high confidence; consistent with humans scoring 57.31% on video largely via semantic cues per HUMAN_DETECTION_BASELINE]. Small vertical phone screens (9:16, roughly 6 inches) further shrink fine-detail visibility, so a shot failing only item 10 often looks clean in-feed [ESTIMATE, moderate-high confidence; [UNKNOWN: no fetched study quantified screen-size detection deltas]]. Honest flip side: compression is not a license to relax entirely - it can also add blocky artifacts that make borderline AI texture look worse. Net doctrine: run final QC on an actual phone at feed resolution, and spend the rubric budget top-down.

the small-screen visibility factor and its UNKNOWN quantification

nodes.definition: Garbled lettering, near-English words, and mixed alphabets on signs, books, or shirts are historically the most reliable single AI-image tell [FACT - via search excerpts]. Newer models can produce clean typography, so absence of garble is not proof of real, but presence of garble is near-proof of AI [FACT - via search excerpt]. For a luxury operation, brand logos (car marques, fashion houses) are high-risk because viewers know exactly what a Rolls-Royce grille badge or an interlocking-C logo should look like [ESTIMATE - reasoning from the text-tell evidence, high confidence]. This is rubric item 1, ranked most damning because it is binary-checkable by any viewer at a glance without expertise, and it is also why legible text/badges sit on the known-hard avoid list for close-ups.

included: garbled/near-English text as the classic tell
excluded: the shot-redesign workaround for legible-text shots (its own node, KNOWN_HARD_AVOID_LIST)

This is rubric item 2. Dexterous hand-object manipulation (pouring, typing, clasping jewelry) is a documented open research problem with dedicated research lines (ManiVideo, hand-object interaction generation) [FACT], which is also why it appears on the known-hard avoid list rather than being treated as merely QC-able.

nodes.definition: A character's eye color, jacket style, or face geometry changing across frames or shots is an industry-named phenomenon, 'identity drift' [FACT - via search excerpts]. nodes.definition: Route each identified tell to the cheapest sufficient fix. FIXABLE BY PROMPT: physics-negative prompting works measurably - PhysVid's local physics conditioning plus negative physics prompts improved VideoPhy physical-commonsense scores roughly 33% over baseline generators [FACT - abstract]; naming lighting singularly and banning visible text/logos in the prompt reduces exposure at the prompt level [ESTIMATE, moderate-high]. FIXABLE BY MODEL/MODE CHOICE: physics adherence varies hugely across models (VideoPhy/VideoPhy-2 spreads; best is not average) [FACT] - A/B per shot-type and keep a per-model failure ledger; image-to-video from a QC-approved start frame locks anatomy, wardrobe, and identity at t=0 [ESTIMATE, high confidence]. FIXABLE BY RE-ROLL: generation is stochastic, so per-seed artifacts differ run to run - re-roll is the cheapest fix for any single rubric-2, and QC should happen before spending on upscale or post [ESTIMATE - standard generative practice]. FIXABLE IN POST: crop or reframe to excise a bad hand or melted edge, punch in to hide border artifacts, color-grade plus film-grain overlay to restore the high-frequency sensor-noise statistics whose absence reads synthetic [ESTIMATE, moderate-high], and speed ramps or whip-pan transitions to shorten the window in which physics can be judged, placed exactly where drift was building [ESTIMATE, moderate-high]; the format's short stitched-shot length is itself protective because temporal artifacts accumulate with duration [FACT for duration-dependence]. nodes.definition: Compose the operational QC loop end to end. Pass thresholds (from RUBRIC_SCORING_GATE): a total of 0-1 passes outright; a total of 2-3 with no single item at 2 is fixable in post only if the offending region is croppable, gradeable, or speed-rampable, otherwise re-roll; any single item at 2, or a total of 4 or more, forces a re-roll regardless of post-fixability. Re-inspection checkpoints: the start-frame image (rubric items 1, 4, 5, 6, 9, 10), the raw generated video (all ten items), and the post-edited reel re-checked at final resolution on an actual phone screen (items 1-4 minimum, since compression and screen size can mask items 7-10 - see COMPRESSION_HONESTY). A shot that fails at the start-frame checkpoint must not proceed to video generation until it is re-rolled or reprompted, because image-to-video inherits and can compound an image-stage failure. The loop closes only when a shot clears every checkpoint at the phone-screen final-resolution pass; a shot that has cycled through re-roll, model-swap, and prompt-fix without clearing is escalated to shot redesign per MITIGATION_MAP.

conflict_axes.name: noticeability_priority_vs_effort_budget
conflict_axes.description: Tension between spending QC effort proportional to documented noticeability versus the temptation to over-invest in easy-to-check-but-low-impact items like skin texture.
poles: spend QC budget top-down by noticeability
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: always spend the rubric budget top-down (text, hands, contact physics, identity first) and treat skin/background as glance-level checks only

conflict_axes.name: automated_critic_vs_human_judgment
conflict_axes.description: Tension between trusting a cheap automated VLM critic's pass/fail verdict and requiring a human in the loop given documented MLLM artifact-judgment misalignment.
poles: trust the VLM critic's pass/fail verdict
require a human to finalize the rubric gate
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use the VLM critic only as a pre-filter; a human always finalizes the gate score on at least the top-four rubric items

conflict_axes.name: wagon_wheel_false_positive_vs_real_slip
conflict_axes.description: Tension between flagging any wheel-speed mismatch as a physics violation and recognizing that stroboscopic wagon-wheel spin is a real, camera-plausible effect at certain shutter/frame-rate combinations.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: check shutter/frame-rate plausibility before flagging; only treat persistent contact-patch sliding as a genuine violation

conflict_axes.name: post_fixable_vs_shot_redesign_only
conflict_axes.description: Tension between attempting a prompt/model/re-roll/post fix and recognizing that a known-hard shot type is documented as an open research problem that iteration will not reliably resolve.
poles: redesign the shot to avoid the tell entirely
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: check the known-hard avoid list first; if the shot type is on it, redesign rather than iterate

conflict_axes.name: prompt_engineering_confidence_vs_hard_limit
conflict_axes.description: Tension between relying on physics-negative prompting's measured ~33% improvement and PhyGenBench's finding that prompt engineering does not fully fix dynamic physics scenarios.
poles: accept prompt engineering cannot fully fix dynamic physics scenarios
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use physics-negative prompting as a first, cheap pass but never treat it as sufficient alone for dynamic-motion shots; keep re-roll/model-swap in reserve

conflict_axes.name: compression_masks_vs_amplifies
conflict_axes.description: Internal tension within the compression doctrine: recompression hides some high-frequency tells (protective) but also adds blocky artifacts that can make borderline texture look worse (destructive).
poles: compression is destructive (adds new blocky artifacts)
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat compression as protective for texture-class items 8 and 10 only, and still QC at final resolution because blocking can amplify borderline flaws

conflict_axes.name: genre_expert_scrutiny_vs_general_baseline
conflict_axes.description: Tension between QC'ing to the general ~55% human-detection baseline and the higher effective detection rate that car/watch/jewelry genre experts apply to object-specific physics details.
poles: QC to the general ~55% detection baseline
QC to the higher genre-expert scrutiny rate for cars/jewelry/watches
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: apply the general baseline as the floor but give disproportionate scrutiny to badges, wheels, and jewelry/watch close-ups

conflict_axes.name: reroll_cost_vs_reroll_cheapness
conflict_axes.description: Tension between budget pressure to accept a marginal shot and the fact that stochastic re-roll is one of the cheapest available fixes.
poles: accept a borderline shot to save generation cost
re-roll because generation is cheap and stochastic
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: re-roll before spending on upscale or post whenever the rubric gate is not clearly passed, since re-roll is cheaper than a wasted post pass

conflict_axes.name: start_frame_lock_vs_video_drift
conflict_axes.description: Tension between trusting a QC-approved locked start frame to carry identity through the whole clip and the fact that identity drift can still accumulate during video generation.
poles: trust the locked start frame carries through
re-check identity every checkpoint despite the lock
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat the start-frame lock as risk reduction, not a guarantee, and still diff identity against the reference sheet at the raw-video and final checkpoints

edge_cases.description: A shot with a stroboscopic wagon-wheel spin gets auto-flagged as a wheel-slip physics violation and is re-rolled unnecessarily.
edge_cases.trigger: wheel rotation appears frozen or reversed at a shutter/frame-rate combination that is real-footage-plausible
edge_cases.mitigation: check shutter-angle/frame-rate plausibility before flagging; only flag if contact-patch sliding persists independent of any stroboscopic explanation

edge_cases.description: A hero champagne-pour shot is scripted and generated despite being on the known-hard avoid list, burning budget on repeated re-rolls that never clear physics QC.
edge_cases.trigger: a hero fluid-pour shot is scripted without checking the known-hard avoid list first
edge_cases.mitigation: check the avoid list at scripting time, before generation, and redesign the shot (imply the pour off-frame) rather than iterate

edge_cases.description: A QC reviewer inspects only on a desktop monitor and passes a shot whose skin-microtexture and texture-boiling failures would have been invisible in-feed anyway, wasting review time on items compression will mask.
edge_cases.trigger: the final QC pass is done on a large monitor instead of a phone at feed resolution
edge_cases.mitigation: run the final checkpoint on an actual phone screen at feed resolution and stop over-weighting texture-class items there

edge_cases.description: An automated VLM critic passes a shot with a garbled logo because MLLM artifact judgment misaligns with human perception.
edge_cases.trigger: only the automated critic reviews rubric item 1 and no human check follows
edge_cases.mitigation: require a human pass on at least rubric items 1-4 regardless of the automated critic's verdict

edge_cases.description: A persona's eye color shifts gradually between several shots in the same sequence and is not caught because reviewers only diff each shot against its immediate predecessor.
edge_cases.trigger: identity is checked shot-to-adjacent-shot but never against the master reference sheet across the whole sequence
edge_cases.mitigation: diff every shot's persona attributes against the master reference sheet, not just against the previous shot

edge_cases.description: A shot scores a single item 2 (a garbled watch face) but the running total is only 2, and a reviewer applying only the total-score threshold passes it.
edge_cases.trigger: the total>=4 rule is applied without checking the any-single-2 override first
edge_cases.mitigation: apply the any-single-2-forces-reroll rule as a hard override before computing the running total

edge_cases.description: Physics-negative prompting is used on a dynamic-action shot and the team assumes the prompt fix guarantees compliance, skipping re-roll or model-swap.
edge_cases.trigger: a prompt-only fix is trusted as sufficient for a dynamic physics scenario
edge_cases.mitigation: treat prompt engineering as risk reduction, not a guarantee, per PhyGenBench's finding, and still apply re-roll/model-choice/shot-redesign fixes

edge_cases.description: A specific object-count-error frequency figure is invented to justify a QC budget allocation decision.
edge_cases.trigger: someone requests a base rate for a specific artifact type that was never fetched
edge_cases.mitigation: state the frequency is UNKNOWN rather than inventing a number, and flag it for future grounding when Artifact-Bench's full 30-type table becomes fetchable

edge_cases.description: A film-grain and color-grade post pass is applied to a shot with a hand-morphing failure, assuming grain will mask it.
edge_cases.trigger: post-grade is used outside its legitimate scope (texture/skin masking) to try to hide a structural or geometric tell
edge_cases.mitigation: restrict grade/grain fixes to texture-class tells (items 8 and 10); geometric/structural tells (hands, contact physics, identity) require re-roll, model swap, or shot redesign

edge_cases.description: A reviewer treats the roughly 55% aggregate human-detection accuracy as license to skip QC entirely because 'audiences can barely tell anyway.'
edge_cases.trigger: the aggregate Diel et al. figure is read as 'audiences won't notice' rather than 'audiences notice worst-case, repeated-exposure tells'
edge_cases.mitigation: apply the worst-artifact-driven per-shot rubric regardless of the low aggregate one-shot accuracy, because repeated posting accumulates exposure

edge_cases.description: A luxury car shot with badge-level detail is passed by general QC without applying the genre-expert-scrutiny uplift, because the reviewer used the general ~55% baseline.
edge_cases.trigger: badge/wheel/watch-face content is QC'd at the general population detection rate rather than the higher genre-expert rate
edge_cases.mitigation: apply disproportionate QC scrutiny to car badges, wheels, watch faces, and logo-bearing goods per the genre-expert-audience reasoning

workflow.action: Establish the human-detection evidence baseline and the automated-critic limitation
workflow.description: State the Diel/Groh/Nightingale-Farid/Miller numbers and the worst-artifact-driven doctrine, then the Artifact-Bench MLLM-limitation finding
workflow.gate: all four studies' headline numbers and the worst-artifact-driven, human-in-the-loop conclusions are stated

workflow.action: Fix the ordered per-shot rubric and its scoring gate
workflow.description: Order the ten tells by noticeability, define the three checkpoints, and set the 0/1/2 scale with re-roll thresholds
workflow.gate: the ten items are ordered, the checkpoints are defined, and the scoring/re-roll thresholds are set

workflow.action: Score the top-priority tells: text/logo and hand-motion
workflow.description: Check for garbled text/logos and finger morphing/object blending against their documented grounding
workflow.gate: both tells are scored with their grounding cited

workflow.description: Check foot/wheel/splash contact physics and diff persona identity against the master reference sheet
workflow.gate: contact-physics is scored against the VideoPhy/VideoPhy-2 grounding and identity is diffed against the reference sheet

workflow.action: Score object-permanence, shadow/reflection, and motion-quality tells
workflow.description: Check object count stability, single-light shadow/reflection geometry, and second-order motion acceleration
workflow.gate: all three tells are scored with their grounding cited, including the D3/NSG-VD/Sora findings

workflow.action: Score texture-stability, background-coherence, and skin-microtexture tells
workflow.description: Check flicker/boiling, background/crowd coherence, and skin waxiness, applying the compression-driven low priority to the last item
workflow.gate: all three lowest-priority tells are scored and the skin-microtexture item's compression rationale is stated

workflow.description: Check wheel rotation, glass/liquid, fabric drape, jewelry sparkle, pool/ocean water, and golden-hour shadows against their must-be-true conditions
workflow.gate: each of the six luxury physics rows states the must-be-true condition, the common AI failure, and its grounding

workflow.action: Cross-check the known-hard avoid list before scripting a shot
workflow.description: Verify the scripted shot is not one of the eight known-hard types before requesting generation, applying the imply-rather-than-show workaround if it is
workflow.gate: the shot is confirmed clear of the avoid list or redesigned with a documented workaround before generation

workflow.action: Route any flagged tell through the mitigation map
workflow.description: Send each rubric-2 item to prompt, model-choice, re-roll, post, or shot-redesign, respecting the PhyGenBench prompt-engineering hard limit
workflow.gate: each rubric-2 item is routed to exactly one fix category with its rationale documented

workflow.action: Run the shot through the three-checkpoint re-inspection loop to close QC
workflow.description: Confirm the shot clears the start-frame, raw-video, and phone-screen final checkpoints, or escalate to shot redesign
workflow.gate: the shot clears all three checkpoints at the phone-screen final-resolution pass or is documented as escalated

priority_rationale: The foundational evidence nodes (human-detection baseline, automated-critic limitation, the ordered rubric, its scoring gate, and the compression-honesty doctrine) come first because every downstream tell and physics check is scored against that shared evidence base and gate. The ten individual tells follow in their noticeability order because each is a distinct unit of expert QC judgment the rubric composes. The six luxury-specific physics checks come next because they are object-class instantiations of the general tells (contact physics, texture, shadow/reflection, motion) applied to the format's signature assets. The known-hard avoid list, mitigation map, and re-inspection loop come last because they compose every upstream tell and physics finding into the operational decisions - what to avoid, how to fix, and when a shot is truly done.

dominance_rules.rule: Any single rubric item scoring 2 dominates the total-score threshold
dominance_rules.rationale: one glaring tell can flip an account's perceived authenticity permanently even if the average shot quality is fine
dominance_rules.trigger: a shot has one item scored 2 but a running total under 4
dominance_rules.action: force a re-roll regardless of the total score

dominance_rules.rule: Noticeability order dominates ease-of-fix when allocating QC attention
dominance_rules.rationale: faces and skin texture are a mostly-won battle while text, hands, and contact physics remain the dominant documented failure modes
dominance_rules.trigger: QC time is limited and must be prioritized across the ten rubric items
dominance_rules.action: spend the rubric budget top-down: text/logos, hands, contact physics, identity, before texture/skin

dominance_rules.rule: A known-hard avoid-list shot type dominates any prompt/model/re-roll/post fix attempt
dominance_rules.rationale: documented open research problems (dexterous manipulation, gymnastics, hero fluid pours) are not reliably fixable by iteration
dominance_rules.trigger: a scripted shot matches a known-hard avoid-list type
dominance_rules.action: redesign the shot (imply rather than show) instead of iterating on generation

dominance_rules.rule: Human judgment dominates the automated VLM critic's verdict
dominance_rules.rationale: Artifact-Bench found MLLM artifact judgments significantly misalign with human perceptual preference
dominance_rules.trigger: an automated critic passes a shot
dominance_rules.action: still require a human pass on rubric items 1-4 before the shot is declared clean

dominance_rules.rule: Phone-screen final-resolution viewing dominates desktop-monitor QC for the pass/fail call
dominance_rules.rationale: compression and small screens hide texture-class tells but not semantic/geometric ones, so desktop QC misweights the rubric
dominance_rules.trigger: a shot is being finally approved for posting
dominance_rules.action: run the last checkpoint on an actual phone at feed resolution

dominance_rules.rule: The master reference sheet dominates shot-to-adjacent-shot comparison for identity checks
dominance_rules.rationale: identity drift accumulates gradually and an adjacent-shot-only check can miss slow drift
dominance_rules.trigger: a persona's identity is being verified across a multi-shot sequence
dominance_rules.action: diff every shot against the master reference sheet, not only the immediately preceding shot

dominance_rules.rule: Documented physics-benchmark failure rates dominate an assumption that a new model has fixed physics
dominance_rules.rationale: VideoPhy-2's best model reached only 22% joint performance on its hard subset, so physics failure remains the norm even for current models
dominance_rules.trigger: a new or updated generation model is adopted
dominance_rules.action: re-run the luxury physics checklist and the motion-quality tell against the new model before trusting it as default

dominance_rules.rule: Camera-plausible stroboscopic effects dominate a naive wheel-speed-mismatch flag
dominance_rules.rationale: wagon-wheel apparent reverse or frozen spin is a real optical effect at certain shutter/frame-rate combinations, not necessarily an AI tell
dominance_rules.trigger: a wheel appears to rotate at the wrong speed
dominance_rules.action: check shutter-angle/frame-rate plausibility before flagging the shot as a physics-violation re-roll

anti_rework_rules.rule: Check the known-hard avoid list before requesting generation, not after reviewing the output
anti_rework_rules.prevents: burning multiple re-roll cycles on a shot type that documented research shows will not reliably clear QC

anti_rework_rules.rule: Apply the any-single-2 override before computing the running rubric total
anti_rework_rules.prevents: passing a shot with one glaring tell because the total score alone looked acceptable

anti_rework_rules.rule: QC the start frame before spending on image-to-video generation
anti_rework_rules.prevents: generating and grading a full video clip whose anatomy/wardrobe/identity failure was already visible and fixable at the image stage

anti_rework_rules.rule: Diff every shot's persona against the master reference sheet, not just the previous shot
anti_rework_rules.prevents: slow identity drift accumulating undetected across a sequence because each adjacent-shot check looked fine in isolation

anti_rework_rules.rule: Restrict color-grade and film-grain fixes to texture-class tells only
anti_rework_rules.prevents: wasting a post pass trying to mask a structural tell (hand morphing, contact-physics failure) that grain cannot fix, then re-rolling anyway

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run final QC on an actual phone at feed resolution before shipping
anti_rework_rules.prevents: shipping a shot that passed desktop QC on skin-texture grounds but reads differently once real platform compression and screen size are applied

anti_rework_rules.rule: Treat physics-negative prompting as risk reduction, not a guarantee, for dynamic-motion shots
anti_rework_rules.prevents: skipping re-roll or model-swap because a prompt fix was assumed sufficient, then discovering the physics violation survived anyway

anti_rework_rules.rule: Re-run the luxury physics checklist against a new generation model before adopting it as default
anti_rework_rules.prevents: silently inheriting a new model's uncharacterized physics failure modes across an entire shot list

iteration_protocol.trigger: a shot fails the rubric gate (single item 2 or total >=4)
iteration_protocol.action: route through the mitigation map: attempt prompt fix, then re-roll, then model swap, escalating to shot redesign if the tell is on the known-hard avoid list

iteration_protocol.trigger: the full 30 fine-grained Artifact-Bench artifact types become fetchable (currently proxy-blocked)
iteration_protocol.action: cross-check the ten-item rubric against the full taxonomy and re-rank items whose base rates change the noticeability ordering

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new generation model or mode is adopted
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the luxury physics checklist and the motion-quality tell against the new model and update the per-model failure ledger before trusting it as default

iteration_protocol.trigger: a shot type repeatedly fails re-roll and model-swap without clearing QC
iteration_protocol.action: escalate to shot redesign, and add the shot type to the known-hard avoid list if it recurs across multiple productions

iteration_protocol.trigger: quantified small-screen detection-delta research becomes available (currently UNKNOWN)
iteration_protocol.action: replace the estimate-based phone-screen doctrine with the measured deltas and re-tune which rubric items are checked at which checkpoint

iteration_protocol.trigger: an automated VLM QC critic's pass/fail history is compared against human review outcomes over enough shots
iteration_protocol.action: recalibrate how much weight the automated critic gets in the pre-filter stage versus requiring a full human pass

iteration_protocol.trigger: identity drift is caught in a shipped post rather than in pre-ship QC
iteration_protocol.action: re-audit the reference-sheet diff step of the re-inspection loop and tighten the identity-lock check at the start-frame checkpoint
